how.server: npx vite --config tools/lighting/vite-lighting.config.mjs --port 6951 --strictPort (dev only, serves the normal maps at /__lightmaps/); stopped afterwards
how.browser: headless Chromium from node on the real GPU (ANGLE d3d11), Playwright; never the browser pane or the Chrome extension
how.route: real keys: Enter on the title, ArrowRight in chapter select to the chapter, Enter in party prep, hold Enter to skip the cutscene, then wait for the first command menu; the run seed is pinned to 1
how.url: ?coach=off&crisp=fplus (the sharpness rung pinned so the frame cannot step down under load); clips add &light=N for looks 1 to 3, today has no light flag
how.stills: at the frozen moment (fx.freeze plus a frozen performance.now) the look is switched at run time with __pyrefly.fx.light.set({mode, strength: 1}); the canvas is read once it stops changing between two grabs; then today is drawn again and its canvas hash must equal the first (it does, in all four sets)
how.clips: DevTools screencast (JPEG q95, about 100 frames a second delivered), resampled to a constant 30 fps and encoded by ffmpeg (VP9 crf 24; GIF with a generated palette); every clip is a fresh page load, same seed, the live battle

moments.ch1: the party's first command menu in the CTB battle (Tidus to act, phase command:tidus); the turn-based battle holds there, so the clip is pure idle
moments.ch4: FFX-2 is Active ATB, so the battle keeps running at the first menu: the stills use the first calm moment after it (phase idle, no damage number on screen, no hit flash), frozen at once; the clips start 0.8 s into that calm moment and run 5 s, so Bahamut's next attack lands in every clip at about the same time (the sim is seeded; the timing can differ by a few tenths of a second between looks)

notes: The sheets read left to right, top to bottom: today, look 1, look 2, look 3. The 2560x1440 sheets are 5186 px wide; the 1600x900 ones 3242.
The canvas sheets leave the HUD out so the figures can be judged alone; the full sheets show the game as played.
The close-up windows are 480x420 pixels cut 1:1 from the 2560x1440 canvas frames; no scaling.
Look 2 normal maps loaded in every look-2 frame (5 figures in Chapter I, 4 in Chapter IV); look 3 halos 5 and 4; stars 4 in every lit look.
No public/art file was written and no ComfyUI job was queued.
